read_scope.notes: Read the complete extracted text of all 22 PDF pages, including references and Appendices A–G; visually inspected all 22 individually rendered pages, Figures 1–5, and Tables 1–12. Consulted only the frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve terminology and source locations. The abstract has 154 whitespace-delimited words after normalizing its TeX accents and punctuation. Treated appendix technical detail as optional depth. No other review, earlier draft, progress record, or external scientific source was consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with consistently interpretable terms. Section 4.1 introduces contrasts through a concrete Monet–Sisley lightness example and explains the two scores with the 1/0/1 benchmark before notation. Qualifications usually identify a specific limitation rather than merely hedge. Local refinements remain in the abstract’s compressed error language and the overlap between the Discussion and Conclusion.
score_reasons.structure: The main text progresses coherently from the ambiguity of a name response to the experiment, feature meanings, estimands, primary comparisons, and retrospective diagnostics. Sections 4.3–4.4 and 5.1–5.5 make the primary/retrospective distinction visible; Table 5 brings the source-correction consequence into the main story. Technical estimators, controls, old cohorts, and provenance are appropriately optional appendices. The Discussion could use its limited space for more synthesis instead of repeating the ordering already established in Table 4.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The question, six prompt conditions, finite digital target, scaling units, noise correction, no-distinction benchmark, and meaning of calibration can all be recovered from the main text alone. Table 1 translates the feature families into observable properties; Figures 1–3 and Table 4 support the central distinctions. The abstract is standalone and within its word limit. Minor terminology in Table 3 and the additive relationship in Figure 4 could be more explicit for readers who inspect displays independently.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet/Sisley example makes the question consequential without claiming perceptual validation. The complete image grid rewards comparison, the Figure 2 detail views expose otherwise hidden painter distinctions, and Figure 3 gives a clear numerical payoff. The Nano Banana/FLUX reversal and the explanation of GPT Image 2’s shrinkage make the results more than a model ranking. A small amount of repetitive closing summary and compressed abstract language slightly reduces the otherwise strong pace.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, supplies both a measured one-coordinate example (.325 versus .254 lightness gaps) and intuitive benchmark generators before introducing the indexed equations.
Section 5.1 and Table 2 separate positive aligned response from low error and distinguish FLUX’s lowest point estimate from established superiority; the benchmark interval is stated transparently.
Figure 1 displays all six conditions for all six models using a stated selection rule. Its caption explicitly distinguishes reference illustrations from generator inputs and matched compositions.

Sections 5.3–5.4 connect the pair diagnostics and changes in ordering to substantive interpretation: alignment can coexist with mismatch, scene averaging can cancel variation, and calibration modifies measured contrasts rather than images.
The source-correction findings are incorporated into Table 5 and the conclusion, including the loss of the Sunburst–FLUX resolution and the retrospective status of the changed comparisons.
The 22-page layout is readable throughout. All main figures and tables are legible, and the detailed appendices do not need to be read to understand the principal findings.

findings.issue: The sentence beginning “All models partly align” introduces “uncalibrated error” before giving the reader a plain-language object of that error, immediately followed by pair alignment, two model orderings, and calibration. These are accurate but densely packed changes of comparison in a 154-word abstract.
findings.reader_effect: A first-time reader can recover the headline but may need to reread the final half to understand how positive alignment and failure against the no-distinction predictor coexist.
findings.suggested_change: Replace that sentence with “All models partly align with reference differences, but uncertainty prevents showing lower overall mismatch than a predictor making no painter distinctions.” Keep the calibration explanation, which is valuable, and avoid adding length; the replacement is shorter than the current sentence.

findings.issue: “Painter-specific” names the residual variation across generated prompt labels, whereas the paper’s core question is whether those label differences agree with the reference painters. Section 5.2 explains the distinction, but the row label by itself is less precise than that prose.
findings.reader_effect: A reader scanning the table can momentarily interpret the 4.3–17.5% component as reference-specific recovery rather than simply departures from the common named response.
findings.suggested_change: Rename the row “Between-name (%)” and replace the caption’s final sentence with “Shared is the four-name mean shift; between-name is departure from it.” This preserves all values and clarifies the display without adding a new analysis or page.

findings.issue: The opening discussion repeats the three model minima from Section 5.4/Table 4, while the conclusion on the same page repeats the common-shift, alignment, calibration, and source-correction findings. The two closing sections partly compete to summarize the same narrative.
findings.reader_effect: The final page spends some of its interpretive space repeating results rather than sharpening what the different estimands reveal.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the model-minimum catalogue with a short synthesis such as “A stronger aligned response can coexist with larger off-target differences. Scene averaging and scalar calibration reveal how consistency and contrast magnitude contribute to the same measured error.” Retain the named numerical results in Section 5.4 and the compact conclusion; this is a substitution or cut, not an expansion.

findings.issue: The plot shows separate aligned-amplitude and orthogonal-residual dots, but its caption does not explicitly say that the two components add to the model’s error D. The identity is available in Appendix B.1.
findings.reader_effect: A reader entering through this optional figure must infer whether the dots are additive components or two alternative error summaries.
findings.suggested_change: Add “The two components sum to D (Equation 4)” within the existing caption, replacing part of the generic opening “Complementary descriptive summaries for the original reference target” to keep the caption no longer.

summary: Excellent editorial communication for a bounded comparison of measured digital reference contrasts. The main study and its principal findings are understandable without technical appendices, and uncertainty, retrospective analyses, source corrections, and lack of perceptual validation are represented carefully. The remaining changes are localized wording, closing synthesis, and display-caption refinements that fit within the existing 22 pages and 155-word abstract limit.
